note_title: Feature request Portal - new idea - Critical
note_text: Hello The product Team, I have a client that want to create weekly, monthly, 6-month and 1-year reports on the tests launched during these periods. The main objective being to realize the performance of the tests through "simple" dashboards which would allow to compare conversions in current week vs week S-1, current month vs month m-1 ... note_text: ---------- Forwarded message ---------De : Erik Beyer <ebeyer@kameleoon.com>Date: mar. 15 juin 2021 à 16:06Subject: Re: Product Release: Kameleoon Horizon has landed!To:  <fdimeglio@kameleoon.com>Hello FabienGreat news and congratulations!I have a following wishes:- Within an experiment: would it be possible to add a few date range possibilities like Google Analytics does?: last 7 days, 14 days, 28 days, 30 days, 90 days, last 12 months- On the experiments-oversight: Would it be possible to add the winner-variation again?Kind regardsErikAm Fr., 11. Juni 2021 um 11:02 Uhr schrieb Fabien Dimeglio <fdimeglio@kameleoon.com>:                                                  Product Release: Kameleoon Horizon has landed!                                                                                  	                                                                                                                                                                        Dear Kameleooners, We told you it was coming and you may have already figured out some of our secrets from the teaser campaign. Kameleoon HORIZON has finally arrived! We won’t say any more, though. We will let you browse and discover the beta version of our new platform.                                                                                                  Discover our new platform                                                                       Important internal note:To know everything about this release, please read carefully this presentation (for internal use only): https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1zX3C1iGgpo9S-5zRlpJ1NlkXHWelesUPVt1NaxdhyDU/edit?usp=sharingA few words about HorizonHorizon is the name given to the release of our new platform that you can access via app.kameleoon.com and which will be replacing our current back-office this summer. After more than two years of research and development, we are now bringing you the Kameleoon of tomorrow: a new platform offering a fluid, intuitive navigation experience and super-efficient campaign management. Here’s a quick overview of the main changes.	                                                                                                                                                                        Manage your campaigns more efficiently From navigation to campaign activation, all the key phases in the user journey have been redesigned so you can manage your campaigns in no time at all.Platform fluidity: We tracked down all the elements that were likely to slow down the loading time of our dashboards. However many campaigns you create, our solution will respond with lightning speed.Simplified menus: Our menus are now more intuitive, having been pared down from eight to four sections and grouped into goal categories (“Activate” / “Explore” / “Configure” / “Administrate") List view: Our dashboards are now displayed as lists for quick identification of your campaigns without needless scrolling.Optimized search: Our search algorithms have been optimized and the search bar is now permanently accessible on our dashboards.Powerful filtering and sorting: With the right-hand panel on your dashboards, you can directly apply many filters. To sort the data displayed, just click on the column headers. Two very useful features for finding the campaign you’re looking for in no time at all. A wealth of information: Want to know more about a campaign? Mouse over the tooltip displayed to the right of the campaign name and you’ll have access to a plethora of detailed information without needing to open our editors or the results page.Actions just a click away: Want to manage campaigns directly from our dashboards? Click on the 3 dots located to the right of each card to access a wide range of actions. You’ll save precious time thanks to the group actions that are already available on our Goals and Segments dashboards.Greater ease of use Comfort is king! Horizon has been designed to give you a pleasant experience that’s adapted to all your uses, whether you’re using a mobile, tablet or desktop.Design system: Our new design system makes the user experience more consistent and intuitive. You’ll find the same components (buttons, colors, behaviors, etc.) throughout. The solution is now also more dynamic and pleasant: it interacts more with its users (notifications, animations, choice of colors, etc.).Responsive dashboards: Whatever device you’re working on, you’ll enjoy an optimal display of your dashboards, so it’s easier to read and manipulate, even when you’re on the move. Creation of personalized views: Do you regularly need to monitor specific campaigns? Or would you like to free up your dashboards from the campaigns that aren’t relevant to you right now? Our new dashboards adapt to everyone’s needs: create a view to save all the applied filters and find it in one click! To see your view as soon as your dashboard loads, simply set it as the default view.Receive a higher level of supportWhatever your level of proficiency with our solution, our Horizon release will help you quickly build on your skills:Onboarding: To start off on the right foot, a guided visit is now available for new users. You can access it at any point via the Help section in the header. Many tooltips have also been added to support you as you navigate the solution.Help Center: Need help? Hop on over to the Help section in the header. Our two documentation websites have been completely redesigned and improved:User manual: https://help.kameleoon.com/Developer documentation: https://developers.kameleoon.com/Note that the migration of this website is not done yet, but is planned today.So, in practice, what’s different today?App: The beta version of our new platform is accessible here: https://app.kameleoon.com. You can create, launch, manage and analyze your campaigns either via this new platform or through our old back-office (which, for the moment, remains accessible and unchanged). For now, our app is only available in English. Only certain pages (including Feature Flag page) and secondary features are not accessible and will be added soon.A/B graphic editor, simulation panel and documentation websites: Discover their new look right now! These will permanently replace their previous versions. And for the icing on the cake, our editor also makes managing tests on mobiles more efficient.Think you’ve found a bug? Don’t hesitate to tell us about it by clicking on “Report a bug” in the Help section. Thanks in advance for your help! What are the next steps?For about a month, our back-office and our app will both be accessible simultaneously. We invite you to take this time to familiarize yourself with our new platform. Over the coming days, we’re going to gradually improve and enrich our app. Before the end of the summer, it will become our only platform, so the days of our back-office are numbered ;-) Of course, we’ll tell you about these changes when the time comes. Stay tuned! Now it’s over to you… head for a new Horizon!We hope you enjoy discovering it. note_text: Hello, I'm Baptiste, a dev from Jean-Baptiste TeamTL;TR: Could we access the binary tree representing the targeting segment from a graphQL query? After discussion with Peter Nikolaev, we found a suitable format and he made a merge request : https://development.kameleoon.net/microservices/ms-core/-/merge_requests/1969One of our web services called mobile bridge used by BPCE needs to be updated.Our webservice retrieves data from a graphQL query : we're getting an element called lightConditions. This element returns an array listing all the conditions linked to the targeting segment but does not indicate the relationship that exists between the elements (if the conditions are linked by an OR or AND operator) and we need this information. We thought that if we had access to targeting in the form of a binary tree like in the Kameleoon.Internals.runtime.personalizations[0]targetingSegment.tree object we could use it to filter the conditions according to our needs.This functionality is important for BPCE, ask Emmanuel Charmat for a more precise evaluation.

note_title: Feature  Request Voting - Integrate Vercel (Like Fastly)
note_text: Close to Fastly. Already integrated by severals competitors: Paired with tools like Statsig, HappyKit, Split, and other experimentation partners, Edge Config can drastically improve performance and load experience. By integrating these tools with Edge Config, their data gets pushed to the edge when it's changed. When a user visits your site, no extra network requests are needed to retrieve the config data. What's more, since the data is globally distributed, latency for the initial read is reduced. Compute before the cacheWhen compute happens instantly, routing decisions can be made before the cache. Making A/B testing and feature flagging possible without added third-party scripts or client-side JavaScript. https://vercel.com/blog/edge-config-public-beta

note_text: Hi Julien and Aurelie, As per our conversation on Friday, I’m sending you this mail in order to show how we used to implement high-workload tickets in Optimize (for example the Jamaica cards). Our way-of-working allowed us to reduce the workload for the dev by not having to hard-code everything manually. We are looking to apply the same procedure in Kameleoon, thus it would be very helpful to us if you could review in detail and see if there is a way to apply the same in KM. In Optimize we would click on the position of the element we would like to changeThe nth of type selector would open and we then would select the type of change (HTML, script, CSS etc.) we want to applyUsually we would go for HTML changes. When clicking on HTML, a window would open allowing us to make the HTML changes As much as possible we would work with image-urls to avoid coding everything manually (for example the header of the entire “text” part of the product card). Following we would select the way how we would insert the new HTML (replace, annex, insert, before).This procedure we would repeat for each element that needs to be replaced/changed. The same procedure we want to apply in Kameleoon. What I understand now, we can use the “edit HTML” button in the configurator. However, sometimes, the “edit HTML” button is not available, so I figured in that case we could use “edit attribute”. However, I’m not seeing how we can define the “way” we want to change the HTML (insert, before, after, annex) and how we can choose the selector for each HTML change.Looking forward to hear from you,

The 100 visits and 20 conversions in the winning variant are achieved much faster than in 8 hours (e.g. in 0.1 hours). In such cases, the adjustment still only happens every 8 hours. => my opportunity costs increaseSolution:- Individual client setting: I can set a time interval for my account that applies to all projects and experiments.- Project individual setting: I can set a time interval for my projects that applies to all experiments in the respective project. (see Perso control group)- Experiment individual setting: I can set a time interval for my experiments that only applies to the individual experiment. (see MBA option itself)

note_text: Setting a specific time for importing XML files on an e-commerce website's recommendations block is crucial for ensuring the accuracy and timeliness of product recommendations. Here's why:Freshness of Data: By setting a specific time for importing XML files, the system ensures that the latest updates from suppliers or product databases are included in the recommendations. This freshness of data is essential for providing customers with up-to-date information about products available for purchase.Relevance to Customers: Customers expect relevant recommendations based on their current interests and preferences. Importing XML files at specific times allows the system to incorporate the most recent data, thereby increasing the relevance of product recommendations. This relevance enhances the overall user experience and increases the likelihood of conversion.Competitive Advantage: In the highly competitive e-commerce landscape, staying ahead with the latest products and offerings is crucial. By importing XML files at specific times, the e-commerce website can ensure that its recommendations feature showcases the newest products, giving it a competitive edge over other platforms that may not update their recommendations as frequently.Accurate Inventory Management: Setting a specific time for importing XML files also aids in accurate inventory management. By regularly updating product information, including availability and pricing, the system can prevent recommending out-of-stock items or displaying outdated prices, which can lead to customer frustration and loss of sales.Optimized Performance: Importing XML files at specific times allows for better resource allocation and system performance optimization. By scheduling imports during off-peak hours or times of low website traffic, the system can minimize disruption to the user experience while ensuring that recommendations are continuously updated and available when customers visit the website.In conclusion, setting a specific time for importing XML files is essential for maintaining the freshness, relevance, and accuracy of product recommendations on an e-commerce website. By prioritizing timely updates, the platform can provide customers with a superior shopping experience, gain a competitive advantage, and drive increased sales and customer satisfaction.

note_text: Hi!  I had a call with a prospect (automotive), and he asked if it was possible to track revenue within Kameleoon. Use case: The visitor has been exposed to Variation A and purchased a car in the car dealership. Answer 1: possible thanks to Data API + Attribution Window + Cross Device Reconciliation. note_text: Many customers work with widgets and the associated experiments. Pain point: So often we get the following bug report: "I have updated the widget, but the old version is in the experiment". If the widget is inserted into an experiment, then the widget is "static". If I change something in the widget, the widget in the experiment isn't automatically updated, i.e. after every widget change I either have to create a new variant in the experiment and add the widget again OR I have to delete the widget in the JS/CSS code pop ups and add the widget again. We are talking about a workaround of 3-5min for each change in the widget.  At the same time, the UPDATE CTA in the Widget Studio actually tells me that I have performed an update. However this update doesn't apply to the experiment where my widget is inserted, but only to the widget itself.

note_text: SRM and Redirects are are big problem for consultant & support.It would be better to tell customer directly, while creating a redirect what they should do and what NOT:https://help.kameleoon.com/url-redirection-split-test/https://help.kameleoon.com/checking-for-potential-srm/#What_causes_SRMPlease check if we could get customers an advice to take care, if they don't follow this rules an SRM could appear!help doc:Check if the experiment is based on a redirectionThis issue arises when some visitors redirected to variant B fail to see the page, or when data collection only occurs after page B loads. This results in data loss for variant B that wouldn’t happen on the original page.⇒ To address this, we recommend:Target only consented visitors using the following code in the targeting:return Kameleoon.API.Visitor.experimentLegalConsent || falseUse the native redirection (under the variation options) OR Kameleoon.API.Core.processRedirect('newURL') instead of document.location.href = “newURL”Don’t target the newURL where visitors are redirected, and ensure Kameleoon is installed on that newURL.Implement a redirection on the original page as well, aligning its behavior with variant B. To set up the experiment effectively, you should have three variants:Variant A: This variant should be disabled, with 0% traffic allocated to it.Variant B: This serves as the new control variant, redirecting to itself (the page URL of the original version).Variant C: This is the variant you want to test.

note_title: check barrier-free access
note_text: Pain Point:   From mid-2025, websites and apps will be legally required to be barrier-free. This is regulated by the Barrier-Free Accessibility Strengthening Act (BFSG). The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) implements the EU directive of the European Accessibility Act (EAA) so that standardised rules on accessibility apply throughout Europe. The regulations are based on the European standard EN 301 549, which in turn is largely based on the international guidelines for accessible web content (WCAG). e.g. sufficient contrast between foreground and background colour, links and buttons operable via the keyboard, screen reader compatibility of a website, etc.   Even if the website offers this accessibility on its live site, there is still a risk that the variant of an experiment or personalisation will not fulfil it. Such a design can have legal consequences and penalties.    Solution:   There are various features in Kameleoon that check for accessibility when changes are made. The contrast check of colours in new editors is a first step and a good example of this.

note_title: Improvement visitor capping
note_text: Pain Points: The capping option "Stop personalization when the total number of exposed visitors exceeds a threshold equal to ???? visitors" works very unexpected. If the customer enters a predefined number of visitors here, then he expects exactly this number of visitors on the result page. However this is currently technically almost impossible, as there are the following inaccuracies:    the capping check runs X hours or minutes. So there is a period of time in which the visitor limit has already been exceeded, but the next check has not yet been performed.   After the start, there is a minimum period of 30 minutes until the first visit is completed. The stop takes place on the basis of this data, i.e. this causes a further time delay.   The script is of course always subject caching.     Solution: Perhaps the check can be run more frequently and the data analysis can be based on the new real time data.

note_title: AND/OR operators for Events & Actions in the Widget Studio
note_text: Pain point: there are always widgets where it would be necessary to link several events together, which then trigger an action. For example as a provider of a domain with several languages, it's necessary to query the browser language or the URL parameter with the reference to the language, e.g. .ch/fr. At this moment I can only assign one or several actions to this event. But I also want to query for the event "click on element" to trigger a specific goal conversion. Solution: In the Segment Builder it's possible to link several conditions using AND/OR operators. This enables the construction of more complex logics. Such a setup for Events & Actions in the Widget Studio would also be helpful. Several actions can already be assigned to an event with the logic of an “AND” operator.

note_title: synthetic method
note_text: I have one interesting question ’ve been asked on the pre-sale, about “synthetic” control method:A synthetic control in the context of A/B testing on the web is a method of analysis that is used to create an artificial control group when a real control group cannot be obtained due to limitations in the experiment. Typically, a synthetic control is used when it is difficult or impossible to conduct a full randomized experiment with a real control group. Instead of relying solely on a real control group, it is possible to create a synthetic control group. This typically uses a statistical method that combines data from other groups, segments, or time to “simulate” the behavior that the control group might have if it existed.  It is easy to sell to a team launching the projects with 100% on Variation. For example: some marketing activities where test is going to diverted and client can not sacrifice traffic for AB tests and still wants so see what additional income they had.

note_title: Raw Data export 2.0
note_text: Pain Points:   Enterprise: A medium/large customer quickly reaches 100k as a data volume in an experiment. Free export is no longer possible for such experiments. Theoretically it could be exported over several months in smaller periods. But this is impractical and inefficient. Such a customer therefore never has the opportunity to make even one complete export. They therefore never get to know the feature and cannot discover any benefits from it. Which is to Kameleoon's disadvantage. In a direct customer comparison this is unfair because a small customer runs 1-3 raw data exports per month (for free), which may also correspond to their output. So a small customer has his raw data for almost every experiment, while larger customers cannot use it without additional costs.    Debugging/CSM: customers build goals, CDs and co. themselves. In addition to qualitative quality management, quantitative quality management is often also useful. This can easily be done via a raw data export. The raw data therefore helps with quality management without having any "direct business added value". Above all if customers don't find mistakes they cannot even go into debugging independently. Because the access to the raw data export is missing/limited. At such times they end up with the CSM. The CSM is now faced with the dilemma of offering the upsell or helping out with a billable export themselves.   Aggregated exports: Customers don't always understand the difference between aggregated and raw data. Nor about the technical efforts & costs behind it. Why one is behind a paywall and the other isn't leads to even more disagreement.   Data authority: Customers find it unfair that their data is deliberately kept behind a pay wall   Transparency: the customer has no transparency about his already exported data points. It could be 0 or 99,999 - they're only informed via a pop-up that they will not receive their export. He doesn't know whether he could possibly receive the export with a small period adjustment. Also the CSM as the first point of contact doesn't know.   All-teams approach: it isn't uncommon for exports to be made sporadically. For customers with several modules, several teams are usually involved, which export independently of each other. It sometimes happens that the FE team “steals” the export budget from the WebEx team without them knowing or being able to oversee it.   User role: There is currently no option to prohibit the export of raw data for some roles. Anyone from marketing to Super Admin can request a raw data export and thus use the “budget”.   Technical customers: the increasing number of feature experimentation customers and due to the all-teams approach leads to more operational contacts with very good technical understanding. For them it's quite obvious that the raw data query has low costs for us and that the pricing therefore contains a very large margin. Answer from a client after he received the pricing: Are your costs for the queries that high? The data is stored in a Cassandra DB regardless of our query limit, right? I would expect such a simple raw data export without complex calculations to cost a maximum of 1€ per query.   Sales: Operational Kameleoon users predominantly don't like sales processes and have no direct budget responsibility. It always creates a bad mood when they receive the limit popup in kameleoon and/or the feedback from CSMs with the 100k limit. Usually the operational processes then come to a standstill. In most cases short-term compromises are then made (with service) and the sales process is started in parallel. This often starts with low customer satisfaction.    Pricing Solutions:   annual budget: The budget is no longer monthly, but annual. This means that each customer could export 1.2 million data points per year until they reach the threshold. As a first upsell, the threshold would be up to 12 million data points per year. Unlimited is retained anyway. (Disadvantage: the upsell of small customers becomes more unrealistic)   The budget isn't by default 100k data points per month for each customer, it's based on the paid MAUs of the existing contracts e.g. 0.5 MAUs = 100k, 1.0 MAUs = 250k, 1.5 MAUs = 500k, 2 MAUs = 750k, .....This ensures that there is budget for debugging and/or that every customer can export at least 1 experiment per month free of charge. If they become a regular user, they will need the upsell. The model would of course also be possible on an annual basis (#1).    Tool Solutions:   progress bar: The number of exported data points is displayed in the Bo, visible to every Kameleoon user (e.g. in the project section). Preferably with a progress bar and the applicable limit.  The popup also shows this view when the limit is exceeded. We build something like this hundreds of times as a shipping cost overview in experiments :)    user role: Only admin and/or production should be allowed to request raw data exports. If other roles try it, the popup should indicate that the correct role has been assigned. Alternatively individual users could also be assigned the "privilege" of raw data export regardless of their role, e.g. a data analyst only has marketing rights but is allowed to export   Tolerance limit: An export that only just exceeds the limit, e.g. 100,387 visits, will still be executed. However the user will receive a clear message that we have been generous and don't want to disrupt their work. It isn't possible to do this again. We are showing goodwill. The tolerance limit can remain secret.   History: similar to changes in experiments, there is an "export history" with date, time, Kameleoon user name and amount of data used. It creates maximum transparency in the team and may also help to better organize the team structure.

note_title: Archive for a goals
note_text: Given that we’ve recently identified an issue where deleting goals from the back office results in the loss of associated data on results pages, I propose implementing an Archive feature for deactivated goals (similar to the existing archiving functionality used for experiments).  Clients periodically need to clear unused segments, custom dates, and outdated goals to streamline access to relevant metrics and maintain an organized workspace. However, since outright deletion risks erasing on a test results, introducing a two-step process — deactivation followed by archiving (deleting archived goals in 2 years automatically)—would preserve data integrity while resolving this challenge. This approach ensures clients retain visibility into past campaigns without compromising the usability of their active dashboards.

note_title: new goal type: sum goal
note_text: Pain Point: As a CRO manager, it is important to me that I set up detailed tracking. I use many secondary goals for this. Sometimes I track more specific and sometimes more general interactions, e.g. purchase of a specific product, purchase of any product from a specific category,...Over time this results in a lot of goals that I can't always reuse. Often there is just a lack of possible combinations. I then have to code these as a new custom goal.  Solution: a new Goal type: Sum Goal.As a user, I can select it in the goal popup dropdown (comparable to click or scroll tracking type).    I can then choose from the list of existing goals in the account. Any number of goals can be selected. My new total goal then always converts when the selected goals convert.       Added value: I can create a portfolio of specific goals. As soon as I need combinations, I can simply click them together. Comparable to multiple selectors with our Goal Type: Click Tracking.

feature_name: Assign visitor to predefined persona for better personnalisation
note_title: 1h talk with Vertbaudet
note_text: AI Subjects & Experiment Requests Next AI Experiment Release:   Request to mix URL analysis and document analysis to summarize the tone of voice.   Tone of voice is critical as it forms the foundation for their text-generation solutions.   Personalization & AI Emotions:   Interested in AI emotions as presented by La Redoute at Monaco.   Find AB Tasty's presentation of AI emotions odd.     Main goal: Kameleoon should create Segments and assign AB tests to those segments.   Segments can be a mix of different personas (e.g., "Future mother" + "Gift").     They dislike the term "hyper-personalization" but want AB tests adapted to particular segments or segment mixes.   AI Opportunities:   Hard to identify clear opportunities.   Wish to have AI opportunities summarized in a centralized place.   Other AI subjects:   Natural Language Processing (NLP) is a key area for Kameleoon to improve on.   Using Generative AI to review and create code; they believe Claude is the best solution.     Other Subjects: Results Page:   Switching from sequential to CUPED to MTC is confusing.   Want a default view that provides relevant results first.     Struggles with stability: sometimes the old results page doesn't load (not an issue on the new one).   New results page presents too much information at first glance.   Code Editor:   Interested in the new code editor; if not GA in April, they should be included in the first wave of clients.   Code areas are too small across most of the platform.   Finalization Flow:   Want the ability to minimize the JS condition in quick targeting (possibly with a chevron).   Simulation:   Thinks it takes too long to load.   CTA is not intuitive; caused panic due to incorrect simulations.   Want the ability to deactivate all other AB tests at once to test ONLY the current one.   ROI & Forecasting:   Want a tool to generate segments with real revenue potential.   Ideally, an algorithm that scans the website and generates segments automatically (without manual prompts).     Like the idea of forecasting campaign contributions to the year’s revenue.   "How can I know the potential of a test over a full year for ALL my visitors?"   Use and like Asana for project management (Kanban views, filtering, etc.).   Awaiting campaign management in Kameleoon.     Appreciate highly configurable dashboards.   Other Platform Considerations:   Discussed data availability on the Home Page, including total profit, potential uplift, etc.

note_title: Kameleoon's Global Product Roadmap - new idea - Important
note_text: Feature Request: Page-Specific CSS Selectors in Graphic EditorAllow users to specify the scope of CSS selectors in the graphic editor to apply modifications only to selected pages, avoiding unintended changes across multiple pages with common selectors.Currently, when using the graphic editor, modifications are applied based on CSS selectors. If a selector is present on multiple pages, the changes affect all instances across the campaign. This becomes an issue when a user wants to apply different modifications to specific pages but cannot do so because the selector is not unique to a single page.For example, on e-commerce sites, product description sections often share the same class (e.g., .ProductDescription). If a user modifies this class in the visual editor, the change is applied globally across all product pages, rather than being limited to a specific set of URLs or product types. This limitation forces users to write custom code to scope their modifications, which is not ideal for those unfamiliar with coding.For now, it seems that the system applies runWhenElementPresent behind the scenes when a CSS selector is chosen in the visual editor. It would be great to have the option to add an includes condition for the page URL, either with a regex pattern or a flat URL match. This would allow non-technical users to easily restrict their modifications to specific pages without having to write custom JavaScript conditions manually.

note_text: Pain Point: As a content client headline and teaser image testing is very interesting for me. Both are crucial in determining whether my content teaser is clicked. note_title: Traffic expose feature for Web Experimentation
note_text: In our Feature Flag experiments, we have the "expose traffic" option, which efficiently divides traffic within a single segment by prioritizing a larger share of users for critical tests. Additionally, there is a feature that assigns priority to FF Rules to further streamline testing. However, neither of these functionalities exists in Web Experimentation. While working with the Leroy Merlin team, we encountered multiple front/backend projects requiring:   Mutually exclusive test setups (to avoid overlap),   Allocation of uneven traffic shares (for targeted distribution).   The absence of these features in Web Experimentation has imposed significant constraints, leading to:   Unnecessarily prolonged testing durations for key experiments.   Inability to prioritize projects with higher CPO values, undermining efficiency.   Ultimately, these limitations may lead clients to launch fewer projects. These two pain points are particularly critical for large-scale clients, as they directly impact scalability and strategic prioritization.

note_text: Concerning the use of the IA Predictive Targeting moduleIn my various discussions with customers on this subject, I've noticed that using the word “Trigger” when configuring the IA Predictive goal doesn't necessarily make sense. In fact, the addition doesn't “trigger” anything, as an action in itself. It's a way of recording data based on one or more key moments in the user journey.This becomes even more complex with the new segment builder, because when an experience is created, this is what happens.In targeting, we select a Predictive AI condition.We select the goal from which we want to load user heat scores + a trigger from the list of associated key moments (to refine the curve we want to use). This trigger doesn't trigger anything in the experiment configuration, it's only linked to the AI goal. BUT you'll also need to add segment OR trigger elements to the experience targeting to indicate when/where/to whom this experience should be displayed. The trigger can be the same as that used for the AI goal, or completely different. In short, I simply note that the use of "trigger" terminology in the experience is hardly palpable in the context of a campaign that uses an AI goal. Perhaps the use of Key Moments, as historically could help make this clearer.

note_text: Description: We would love to see a feature in Kameleoon that allows us to host small backend tasks or microservices directly within the platform. One practical use case would be to call a microservice that checks whether a user's postal code qualifies for a same-day delivery message, without the need to set up separate infrastructure.Benefits:No need to manage separate servers or cloud functionsStronger integration with Kameleoon’s existing workflows (e.g. server-side experiments or feature toggles)Faster iteration thanks to centralized setupLikely easier to handle from a legal/compliance perspective, since everything stays within the Kameleoon environmentConclusion: This feature would clearly differentiate Kameleoon from other A/B testing platforms and significantly increase flexibility and speed in implementing experiments.

It would be highly valuable to also have the ability to bulk edit project permissions and account permissions.Why it matters:	•	Managing larger organizations with many users is time-consuming when permissions need to be updated one by one.	•	With account permissions specifically, it would be very helpful to bulk edit solutions (e.g., enable/disable Web Experimentation or Feature Experimentation) for multiple users at once.	•	This would reduce admin overhead, improve consistency, and make it easier to onboard or adjust access for entire teams.Proposed functionality:	•	Extend bulk edit options beyond deactivate/delete.	•	Allow selection of multiple users to update:	•	Project permissions (product/marketing/technical/admin)	•	Account permissions, including toggling solutions (Web Experimentation, Feature Experimentation).This would save significant time for admins, reduces risk of inconsistent permission setups, and improves scalability for organizations managing dozens or hundreds of users.

note_title: Kameleoon's Global Product Roadmap - new idea - Critical
note_text: API Feature Request: Programmatic Access to Feature Flag / Experiment Activity LogUser Story:As an API user, I want to retrieve the full historical activity log for each feature flag and experiment, including events like 'paused', 'resumed', 'archived', and changes to traffic allocation.Business Value & Use Case:The excellent "Activity Log" feature is currently available in the Kameleoon UI, but this data is not exposed through the public API. Programmatic access to this log would unlock several key capabilities for us:Automated Auditing & Compliance: For compliance and incident review, we need to maintain a programmatic record of when experiments are activated or deactivated in our production environment.Real-time Alerting: We want to build automations that trigger alerts in our internal systems (like Slack or PagerDuty) whenever the state of a critical feature flag is changed.Performance Correlation: Access to these event timestamps would allow us to automatically correlate experiment pause/resume events with our internal performance metrics (e.g., site latency, error rates) to quickly understand the impact of any changes.Currently, the API only provides the dateModified timestamp, which doesn't specify what changed. This requires us to perform manual checks in the UI, which is not scalable for our monitoring and auditing needs.Suggested Solution:A potential solution could be a new endpoint, for example: GET /feature-flags/{featureKey}/activity-log.This endpoint could return a list of event objects, each containing details like the timestamp, the user who made the change, the action performed (e.g., 'paused_rollout_rule'), and any relevant details.Exposing this data via the API would significantly enhance our ability to integrate Kameleoon into our automated DevOps and compliance workflows.

note_title: Mobile Exit-Intent Trigger
note_text: Context On desktop, Kameleoon provides a native mouse-leave exit-intent trigger.However, no equivalent trigger exists on mobile, because there is no mouse cursor. To show exit-intent pop-ins on mobile, we currently need to implement several custom scripts and workarounds. Requested Feature 👉 Add a built-in “Mobile Exit-Intent” trigger in Kameleoon, similar to the desktop exit-intent trigger, but based on mobile-friendly signals. Suggested Behavior The mobile exit-intent trigger would fire when one or more of the following signals are detected:   Back-button pressWhen the user taps the browser/app “back” button (captured via popstate).   Tab/App switch (page becomes hidden)When visibilitychange fires and the page switches to hidden.   Fast upward scrolling   Why this matters   It would allow brands to trigger pop-ins on mobile at the right moment, boosting conversion and lowering bounce rate.   It removes the need for complex custom JavaScript.   It creates feature parity between desktop and mobile.   It ensures consistent behavior across browsers (iOS/Android).   Expected Usage This new mobile exit-intent trigger should be available:   as a standard targeting condition in Kameleoon, or   as a built-in trigger event in the widget builder.
